correctness.rationale: Lifting a monotone crown map to the infinite alternating fence gives increments in {-1,0,1} whose total is 2n times the degree and bounds absolute degree by floor(m/n). Between nonzero increments every zero run has even length. Comparable-map moves cancel adjacent opposite signs and slide zero pairs, reducing every nonextremal fixed-degree map to a common sign-pure normal form and using a spare zero pair to connect target phases. At maximal degree when n divides m, every increment has the same sign, leaving n target phases for each sign and no comparable perturbation, hence isolated maps. Fresh exhaustive mapping-poset replay gives map/component totals 48/1, 200/3, 234/7, 1156/7, and 1248/3 for the five representative pairs, with degree-resolved component sizes exactly as predicted.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge originality passes with a substantial close-analogy risk. Cavallo-Sattler define the same crown winding number and prove only the shorter-to-longer zero-degree bound. Cukic-Kozlov classify connected components of graph-Hom complexes between ordinary cycles by wrap data and isolate maximal wraps, but graph homomorphisms forbid collapsing a source edge, whereas monotone crown-poset maps may collapse comparable pairs; their complex is therefore not the finite-space mapping poset. The assigned cancellation/zero-pair argument is the missing bridge that classifies all monotone maps. The older Farley and Currie-Visentin papers explicitly enumerate raw order-preserving maps but their full text was inaccessible in this run; authorized institutional attempts after OA failure were unavailable, so no whole-document noncoverage claim is made.
residual_risks: The inaccessible Farley and Currie-Visentin full texts remain a material originality risk.
The graph-Hom cycle theorem is structurally very close; an unlocated published bridge from collapsible poset maps to its components could reduce originality.

value.rationale: This is a complete two-parameter classification for the standard finite T0 models of the circle. It identifies every realizable degree, a sharp divisibility boundary, and the exact rigid maximal-winding multiplicity, providing concrete finite-space information that ordinary topological homotopy and graph-Hom analogues do not by themselves supply.

final_claim: For crown finite-space circle models \(C_m,C_n\) with \(m,n\ge2\), the realizable degrees of monotone maps are exactly the integers \(d\) with \(|d|\le\lfloor m/n\rfloor\); every nonextremal degree gives one homotopy class, while if \(n\mid m\) each extremal degree has exactly n isolated maps, giving the stated divisibility-sensitive total class count.
limitations: The theorem concerns pointwise finite-poset homotopy of monotone crown maps, not graph-Hom complexes or arbitrary finite models of the circle.
